items.event_time_ist: Wednesday, Oct 21, 2026 — meeting outcome reported ~2:58 PM CET (12:58 PM UTC), talks ran ~10:30 AM–1 PM CET
items.summary: CGT secretary-general Sophie Binet emerged from 2.5 hours at Matignon saying Sébastien Lecornu announced 'aucune mesure' (no measures) and there was 'no consideration' of union demands on purchasing power, wages or services. The CGT — which backed the Oct 17 day of action — confirmed it will be back in the street on Saturday Oct 24 'to accompany and protect' those who march at the yellow vests' 'Act II', and called for 'a new cap': 'the strike must take over' at the near-total union day on Nov 5. CFDT's Marylise Léon demanded 'social answers'. Student and lycée organizations were not invited; the education minister will receive them Monday. Macron, from Doha, offered no social announcements but demanded 'firmness' against rioters ('la main ne doit pas trembler'). Hollande slammed a 'weak' government and 'absent' president; Philippe criticized the Gulf trip; Le Pen denounced 'a finishing power'.
items.title: Oct 21: Matignon union talks end empty-handed — CGT joins Oct 24 marches, calls for strike escalation on Nov 5

items.event_time_ist: Tuesday evening, Oct 20, 2026 (statements reported in AFP wire published Oct 21)
items.summary: Paris prosecutor Laure Beccuau said Tuesday evening that of the 557 people taken into custody in Paris over the Oct 17-18 violence and looting, about 300 have so far appeared before a magistrate — and none of them 'claimed any political motive whatsoever', undercutting the government's claim that the 'ultragauche' orchestrated the chaos. Separately, the Défenseur des droits (rights ombudsman overseeing police ethics) announced Tuesday it has received 46 complaints since the start of the lycée movement, 'more than ten' concerning the weekend.
items.title: Oct 20 evening: prosecutor says no Paris suspect claimed a political motive; rights ombudsman logged 46 police-ethics complaints

items.event_time_ist: Tuesday evening, Oct 20, 2026 (announced at a supporters' conference)
items.summary: Jean-Luc Mélenchon told supporters Tuesday evening that La France insoumise will attend the political-parties meeting convened by Sébastien Lecornu at Matignon on Thursday Oct 22 — but intends to sabotage it: 'On va y aller, on va te pourrir la réunion' ('We're coming, and we're going to spoil the meeting'). He mocked Lecornu's invitation letter — which asks parties to condemn violence and puts presidential-campaign security on the agenda — as 'a very strange meeting', rejecting any pledge to sign a commitment on violence. LFI had been silent on the invitation until now. RN's Le Pen/Bardella are skipping Thursday's meeting.
items.title: Oct 20 evening: Mélenchon confirms LFI will attend Thursday's Matignon parties meeting — 'and spoil it'

items.source_name: Ma Vigilance (citing AFP via Sud Radio)
items.summary: The intersyndicale of professional firefighters extended their strike — in place since Sept 8 and set to expire Oct 20 — through Dec 4 inclusive, judging the government has not answered their demands. Parallel labor pressure track to the cost-of-living movement.
items.title: Oct 21: firefighters' strike extended through Dec 4
